thread:
maria: Heads up — onboarding flagged a mismatch between the console and actual alert delivery. When a tenant SLO has per-entity notify + quiet_window set, the console shows "primary-oncall" but the alert actually goes to a reserve channel. Anyone seen UI vs router disagree? :thinking:

ash: Yeah, seen that before. My guess: the frontend shows the declared routing (what the SLO config says) but not the effective route after quota/quiet-window/fallback logic. The routing shim composes fanout + quota and can rewrite targets.

sam: Can you paste the SLO rule JSON here? quick look might show a missing field that explains the fallback.

maria: Sure — snippet (redacted tenant id):
```json
{
  "slo_id": "s-xyz",
  "threshold": 0.99,
  "notify": {
    "route_hint": "primary-oncall",
    "per_entity": true,
    "quiet_window": {"start": "23:00", "end": "06:00"}
  },
  "fallback_policy": "notify-fallback-v2"
}
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout "v2-route-shim" to prod completed (c8a1f2) :white_check_mark:

jules: I think the key is that the notify-fallback step will rewrite the target to `reserved-pager` if the tenant exceeded notify quota or is in quiet-backoff. The console currently only renders `notify.route_hint` and doesn't surface the fallback reasons. So the UI is accurate for the declared config but not the effective delivery.

kevin: Two product choices: (A) show both declared and effective routing in the SLO card (recommended for transparency), or (B) change the API so the frontend requests the effective target from the router before render. Option B is more accurate but heavier.

ash: Option B has a perf concern — effective routing requires querying the quota/eval engine which is a slow path. We could add a routing-index (cached view of last computed effective routes) updated near-real-time. That keeps page loads snappy.

sam: Low-effort workaround: add a "Preview effective route" button in the editor that calls the full routing evaluation for a single tenant sample. That avoids extra calls on every page load and helps on-boarding to confirm behavior.

maria: I like the preview idea as short-term. Longer-term, showing declared vs effective is ideal. Also we need telemetry: how often does UI-declared != delivered? We should emit an event when fallback rewrites a target and correlate with SLO id + tenant + fallback_reason.

jules: +1. I'll open a telemetry PRD: dimensions: tenant_id, slo_id, declared_route, effective_route, fallback_reason, quiet_window_active, and timestamp. We can add a rule-run counter so we can estimate impact.

kevin: Action items: maria — file UX ticket for declared vs effective and add preview mock. jules — telemetry PRD + alert if mismatch rate > 0.5% per tenant. ash — feasibility spike for routing-index (cache API + TTL). sam — mock preview UI and localization copy for tooltip. I'll schedule a short sync Wed 10:00 to align.

maria: Filed UX ticket: https://redwood-internal/issue/PLAT-4872 — tagged @design @frontend. Adding a note to onboarding doc for now.

ash: I'll start a 2d spike to prototype routing-index and post findings in this thread.

sam: I'll drop a small prototype of the "Preview" button in the staging build by EOD tomorrow.

jules: Telemetry ticket up: https://redwood-internal/telemetry/RTX-332 (includes sample events).

kevin: Thanks all. If anyone notices other mismatches please paste a sample thread here so we can triage. :pray:
